errors.description: The hem slant measures roughly 6-7 degrees across the leg, whereas the blueprint's red hem line is drawn at closer to 10 degrees.
errors.expected: Hem line running downhill across the leg, as drawn.
errors.actual: Hem edge falls about 70px over 605px of leg width - visibly slanted and clearly not level, but shallower than the schematic.
errors.correction: Accepted as correct in kind. Technical drawings exaggerate this angle for legibility; a real slanted hem falls roughly 1-1.5 cm across a 20 cm leg, which is what the render shows. Forcing the schematic's angle would produce a physically wrong garment, and the brief forbids inventing tailoring detail.

lockedFeatures: Plain uncuffed hem with NO turn-up band (correctly distinguished from the 4.4 cm and 5.1 cm cuffed siblings) - CORRECT
Hem edge visibly SLANTED, running downhill across the leg rather than level - CORRECT, and the whole point of this option against the level-hem siblings
Pressed front crease running the full length of the leg into the hem - CORRECT
Deep inner edge fold hidden inside, hem edge clean with no visible external band - CORRECT
Detail/side orientation of the lower leg, matching the blueprint's magnified hem view - CORRECT
Red hem line rendered in cloth colour only, never as red cloth - CORRECT
Zero annotation: no numbers, arrows, leader lines or text - CORRECT
notes: The blueprint's red line marks the hem/fold line and runs visibly downhill; the render reproduces a slanted, uncuffed hem in cloth colour with the correct downhill direction. Directly comparable against suit-2pc/hem-double-turnup in the same batch, whose hem is dead level - a customer could tell the two apart instantly. The 7.0 cm fold depth is internal and not directly verifiable from an exterior photograph; nothing in the render contradicts it.
